newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai mulls selling two trln won assets.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai mulls selling two trln won assets.

text.p: The Hyundai Group is considering selling assets in the second half of this year in order to generate two trillion won to improve the financial structure of the conglomerate, a group spokesman said.
The spokesman said the group was also studying a plan to raise another one trillion won by offering rights issues in its affiliates.
"We are just considering the plan. Nothing concrete has yet been decided," said the spokesman without elaborating.
The Maeil Business Newspaper said heavy investment in the group's auto and electronics units had prompted the plan.
The daily said Hyundai Group was also trying to improve its financial position. It has the highest debt-to-equity ratio level out of the nation's top five conglomerates or chaebol.
Figures from the Fair Trade Commission showed the debt-to-equity ratio of Hyundai Group rose to 437 percent last year against 376 percent a year ago.
The newspaper said the group would offer rights issues in major affiliates including Hyundai Motor.
It said other major chaebols were expected to follow Hyundai's lead.
